note: Collection names and research leads are based on official online holdings guides or published FRUS source notes. Rooms and puzzles are fictional training exercises. A finding-aid lead is not a retrieved document, an online listing is not full release, and these side quests do not change the scope or status of a FRUS volume.

excluded.fdr: No NSC wing: the NSC was established in 1947, after Roosevelt’s presidency.

dungeons.title: Truman NSC Registry
dungeons.handle: NSC staff files and President’s Secretary’s Files

challenge.question: The Truman guide notes overlapping documents in these two file groups. How do you log them?
challenge.correct: Keep both archival locations and compare the copies.
challenge.wrong: Merge them into one invented collection.

dungeons.title: Ann Whitman Vault
dungeons.collection: Papers as President, 1953–61 (Ann Whitman File), NSC Series
dungeons.handle: NSC meeting records in the Ann Whitman File

challenge.question: You need the presidential NSC series. Which request preserves the hierarchy?
challenge.correct: Ann Whitman File → NSC Series; verify the meeting and folder.
challenge.wrong: Any Eisenhower file with national security in its title.

dungeons.title: Crisis Correspondence Vault
dungeons.collection: National Security Files: USSR, Khrushchev Correspondence, Cuba

challenge.question: For late-1962 correspondence, the library gives this box range and folder date span. What belongs in your lead?
challenge.correct: The published box range and exact folder dates; verify the specific container.
challenge.wrong: A guessed single box number within the range.

dungeons.title: Berlin Country Files
dungeons.collection: National Security File, Europe and USSR Country Files
dungeons.handle: National Archives Identifier 580807; Germany and Berlin folders

challenge.question: NARA lists Germany and Berlin folders within this series. How do you request them?
challenge.correct: Keep series NAID 580807 and verify each folder and date.
challenge.wrong: Call every Germany folder a Berlin decision memorandum.

dungeons.title: Heads of State Vault
dungeons.collection: National Security Council Files: Presidential Correspondence

challenge.question: DANN-E has moved the Uruguay correspondence lead into a general country pile. Restore its citation.
challenge.correct: NSC Files, Presidential Correspondence, Box 765, Pacheco correspondence, September 1970.
challenge.wrong: NSC Files, unknown box; all Uruguay papers have the same provenance.

dungeons.title: West Wing Vault
dungeons.collection: National Security Adviser, Kissinger-Scowcroft West Wing Office Files, 1969–1977
dungeons.handle: High-level diplomacy spanning Nixon and Ford

challenge.question: Why can this Ford Library collection include Nixon-era records?
challenge.correct: These working files remained available and became part of the Ford papers.
challenge.wrong: Every document held at Ford must have been created after August 1974.

dungeons.title: Brzezinski Country Vault
dungeons.collection: National Security Affairs, Brzezinski Material, Country File

challenge.question: The published source note calls this an uninitialed copy. What should your notes preserve?
challenge.correct: Box 14, folder Cuba 7–8/79, and the uninitialed-copy qualification.
challenge.wrong: Describe it as a signed original because it appears in FRUS.

dungeons.title: Executive Secretariat Vault
dungeons.collection: Executive Secretariat, NSC: Country File: Records, 1981–1985
dungeons.handle: Soviet Bloc Economic & Financial Situation Updates

challenge.question: The inventory separates OPEN from OPEN / DIGITIZED. How do you plan retrieval?
challenge.correct: Record the status for each dated folder; open does not guarantee an online scan.
challenge.wrong: Treat every open folder as fully digitized.

dungeons.title: Scowcroft Policy Vault
dungeons.collection: National Security Council records and staff files
dungeons.handle: Brent Scowcroft, Robert Gates and defense-policy staff records

challenge.question: The FRUS sources guide identifies several NSC offices. How do you compare their evidence?
challenge.correct: Keep adviser, deputy and staff provenance distinct while tracing the same issue.
challenge.wrong: Attribute every NSC staff paper to President Bush.

dungeons.title: African Affairs Vault
dungeons.handle: FOIA 2006-0192-F; NSC Director of African Affairs records on Rwanda

challenge.question: What date and office scope belongs in this research lead?
challenge.correct: MacArthur DeShazer, NSC African Affairs, Rwanda, 1993–1994.
challenge.wrong: All Clinton-era Africa policy, 1993–2001, fully represented.

dungeons.title: NSC Records Access Vault
dungeons.collection: NSC RAMS packages: Millennium Challenge Account

challenge.question: NARA lists case 2015-0261-F in a proposed release. What is safe to record?
challenge.correct: Keep the case and dates; a proposed release is not proof of current access.
challenge.wrong: The case number proves every NSC record is open.
